newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PARLT PASSES NEW BANKING LAW.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PARLT PASSES NEW BANKING LAW.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Wednesday passed on second and final reading a new Banking Law which will regulate banks' operation under a currency board system to be introduced on July 1.

"This law, along with the central bank law (voted earlier) is designed to put the banking system back on track and lays the foundation for stabilisation," head of parliament's budget and finance committee Yordan Tsonev told the assembly.

The law aims to strengthen bank supervision and minimise risk of bank failures, he added. One third or 17 of Bulgaria's banks are now in receivership and their insolvency is sought by the central bank through the courts.

The law, due to come in force after being published in the State Gazette, raises the capital requirements for bank licensing to 10 billion levs from current 2.2 billion levs. The capital is to be paid in money.

The previous Banks and Lending Law, which becomes invalid after the new law comes in force, allowed the licensing capital to be paid in collaterals, government securities and other debt instruments, which led to the creation of many weak banks, which collapsed later.
The new law requires banks to disclose account information to the police and National Investigation Service on companies with state or municipal majority participation.
Banks are also required to publish balance sheets every six months. Loans and interest which are 90 days overdue are excluded from the assets until they are paid back.
Loans which are not paid on the due date can be collected with a court order, the law says. So far banks could only sue their debtors, which took years under the cumbursome local legal system.
The law requires banks to participate in a deposit guarantee fund.

Banks can not remain in receivership longer than two months after the new law is enacted if the central bank has not revoked their licenses. Very few of the banks placed in receivership had their licenses retracted so far.
Central bank restrictions and license retractions can not be appealed in court and all appeals filed so far are considered ineffective under the Banking Law.
Bulgaria revamped its financial laws as part of preparations to introduce a restrictive monetary mechanism pledged in a reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
The 1997 budget is the last of laws parliament needs to finalise before the start of the currency board. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
